MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT No. PS-MSA-2026-003 This Master Supply Agreement (the "Agreement") is made between Accord Healthcare, Inc. (the "Supplier") and Gulf Health Purchasing Consortium (a fictional UAE group purchasing organisation) (the "Buyer"), effective 1 January 2026 (the "Effective Date"). 1. PRODUCT AND TERRITORY 1.1 The Supplier shall supply Carboplatin Injection 10 mg/mL (450 mg/45 mL multi-dose vials) (the "Product") manufactured at the Supplier's approved facility in India. 1.2 Territory: United Arab Emirates. Delivery terms: DAP Dubai (Incoterms 2020). 2. FORECASTS, ORDERS AND LEAD TIME 2.1 The Buyer shall provide a rolling 6-month non-binding forecast. Purchase orders shall be placed against the forecast. 2.2 Lead time: the Supplier shall deliver each purchase order within 45 calendar days of order acceptance. 3. LATE DELIVERY 3.1 If any delivery is late, the Supplier shall pay liquidated damages of 0.75% of the value of the late consignment per week of delay, capped at 10% of the annual contract value, without prejudice to the Buyer's right to procure substitute product at the Supplier's cost. 4. EXCLUSIVITY 4.1 Nothing in this Agreement obliges the Buyer to purchase exclusively from the Supplier; the Buyer may qualify and purchase from second and third sources at any time. 5. SUPPLY CONTINUITY 5.1 In the event of a supply shortage, the Supplier shall allocate available Product among its customers on a pro-rata basis by trailing 12-month volume. 5.2 The Supplier shall maintain consignment safety stock equal to 30 days of forecast demand in a bonded warehouse in Dubai (Jebel Ali Free Zone or DAFZ). 5.3 The Supplier shall notify the Buyer within 5 business days of any FDA Form 483, Warning Letter, Official Action Indicated classification, import alert or recall affecting the Product or its facility. 6. PRICE 6.1 Prices are fixed for the first 12 months of the Term. Thereafter adjustments are limited to the UAE CPI change, capped at 3% per year. 7. QUALITY, SERIALISATION AND RECALLS 7.1 The Product shall be manufactured in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practice and the marketing authorisation registered with the UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention. 7.2 Each pack shall carry GS1 DataMatrix serialisation compatible with the Tatmeen track-and-trace platform. 7.3 The Supplier shall bear all costs of any recall caused by a quality defect attributable to the Supplier. 8. FORCE MAJEURE 8.1 Force Majeure shall mean natural disasters, epidemics declared by the WHO and acts of government that are not reasonably foreseeable at the Effective Date. Regional conflict, shipping-lane or airspace disruption in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz are deemed FORESEEABLE and do NOT constitute Force Majeure; the Supplier shall re-route via alternative ports (Khor Fakkan, Fujairah, Sohar) or alternative air hubs at its own cost. A party invoking Force Majeure must give notice within 48 hours and present a mitigation plan within 5 days. 9. The Supplier may not terminate for convenience during the first 24 months. 10. DATA PROTECTION 10.1 Each party shall process personal data in accordance with Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 (UAE PDPL). 11. GOVERNING LAW 11.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Emirate of Dubai and the federal laws of the UAE; disputes are referred to the DIFC Courts.
